claim_boundary: External observations are retained in their native measurement classes. Cross-source derived values are descriptors, not an overall framework ranking and not a GREMLIN superiority claim.

sources.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration Frameworks Benchmark: CrewAI vs LangGraph vs AutoGen
sources.methodology: Same AWS m6i.4xlarge hardware, GPT-4o via Azure OpenAI, temperature 0, 50 executions per task suite.

sources.title: GraphWorkflow: A Low-Overhead Compile-Once Graph Execution Engine for Multi-Agent Systems
sources.methodology: No-op nodes isolate framework overhead; five topologies, 10/50/200 nodes, 9 timed samples after warmups, open harness/raw data.

sources.title: Beyond Prompts: Measuring and Optimizing LLM Tool-Agent Harnesses
sources.methodology: Fixed target inner model, held-out scorecards, repeated optimizer runs, BFCL multi-round and tau2 Retail/Telecom; reports reliability and cost diagnostics.

sources.title: tau2-bench / current tau benchmark repository
sources.methodology: Policy-constrained tool-agent-user tasks with environment-based scoring; benchmark versioning/task fixes must be pinned for comparability.

observations.note: Lift is over the paper's native Deep Agents baseline on held-out scorecards; benchmark-specific scores are not directly comparable across datasets.

observations.observation: Current tau benchmark lineage evaluates policy-constrained tool use with environment-based success; task/version pins are required because fixed tasks can change comparability.

gremlin_bindings.reason: Use no-op nodes and matching chain/wide/diamond topology sizes to isolate GREMLIN orchestration overhead.
Same-model/same-hardware repeated runs provide a practical framework-overhead reference class.
Demonstrates that a runtime harness around a fixed model can produce held-out gains without weight changes; GREMLIN still needs its own actual same-model receipts.
Use a standard environment-based scorer instead of synthetic task quality once an external model endpoint is available.
